# YM47: 藻园 Zao Yuan, "Ts'ao Yuan, Garden of Aquatic Grasses"

Wave 2 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM47` · Page: `/scenes/#YM47` · Row: `research/buildings/YM47-zao-yuan/`

## What it was

藻园 Zao Yuan, west of 长春仙馆 beyond the south-west gate, in the south-west corner of the garden: the five-bay 旷然堂 Kuangran Tang, 贮清书屋 behind, 夕佳书屋 on the pool east of it, 镜澜榭 a little north, the tower 凝眺 and 怀新馆 south-east, 湛碧轩 north-west, 湛清华 south-west (S05 j81:8b-9a). Not one of the Forty Scenes; Malone found a brick dated 1751 on the site (E2258, S02), and S361 dates it to about mid-Qianlong, adding 溜琴亭, 自远轩, a thirteen-bay boat dock with a route to 畅春园, and 粹藻楼 (E2259). The garden was burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188), but a building of the scene (E0451 ties it 'sure'; 藏舟坞 Cangzhou Wu, the boat dock, is the likely one) stood among the 17 buildings 刘敦桢 listed as left after the fire in 1933 (E0451, S337).

From the inventory row: **built** brick dated 1751 found on site (S02 p.81 n.); 1752; **destroyed** 林渊锦镜 survived 1860; later loss (S05, S02, S42, S01, S337).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Not one of the Forty Scenes of 1744.

### How later sources differ

S360's compiler calls 藻园 a staging point between the garden and the western parks, mostly small studies and open halls; dated poems 1759-1798 for 藻园, 怀新馆, 夕佳书屋, 旷然堂, 晴望楼, 履吉斋 (S360). 怀新馆 faces north in the south court of 凝眺楼 (S360).

## What survives today

The 1994 auger survey by the 北京市文物研究所 ahead of a planned miniature-park scheme found the 藻园 buildings ranged round a boat dock in an L-shaped zone about 105 m N-S by 95 m E-W; the same campaign covered 十三所 and 山高水长 (S156).

Surveyed and cleared in 1994 (S981, S156): the buildings lie round a boat dock in an L plan of about 105 m north-south by 95 m east-west (E2263, S156).
